validity.recommendation: No change to Status/PipelineType. Record in ResearcherNotes that Adelphia Gateway is a CONVERSION project: an existing ~84.2-mile former oil pipeline (18-inch, built 1970s under PA PUC jurisdiction, transporting gas exclusively on its northern 34.8-mile segment since 2014) plus a 4.4-mile 20-inch pipeline (installed 2002, already gas), purchased and converted to FERC-jurisdictional interstate gas transmission service by Adelphia Gateway, LLC (NJR subsidiary) under FERC Docket CP18-46 (filed 2018-01-12; amended CP18-46-001, 2018-08-31), plus ~4.7 miles of new-construction laterals (Parkway 0.3 mi, Tilghman 4.4 mi). This explains why ProposalYear/ConstructionYear (tied to the 2017-2018 FERC conversion docket) and the pre-existing pipeline's original construction era legitimately differ, and why EIA's project record (4.75 mi, $143M) covers only the new-construction/conversion scope, not total system length.
validity.researcher_notes: Existence/classification/duplicate confirmed: this is a real, single, non-duplicate operating interstate natural gas transmission pipeline (Adelphia Gateway Project / Adelphia Gateway Pipeline), FERC Docket CP18-46, Adelphia Gateway, LLC (subsidiary of New Jersey Resources), completed into service 2022-12-16 per EIA and FERC. No other GEM PID in this batch roster represents the same asset. Sources: FERC Environmental Assessment (Docket CP18-46, Jan 2019); NJR FY2025 10-K (filed 2025-11-20); EIA dated release (see below); naturalgasnow.org (2019-01-08).

validity.recommendation: Correct Capacity from 250.00 MMcf/d to 850.00 MMcf/d. The recorded 250 is the as-originally-filed (Jan 2018) capacity-addition figure for one segment only; the certificated, in-service total system capacity is 850 MMcf/d (250 MMcf/d added on the southern end of the existing mainline + 250 MMcf/d added on the northern end + 350 MMcf/d unchanged on the existing 20-inch pipe).

Likely origin of the sheet's 250 figure: the January 2018 as-filed application's initial ask (matching a 2018 Pipeline News/PGJ 'Planned Projects' listing showing 'Capacity: 250 MDth/d' for the then-pending project) or a miscopy from NGN's unrelated '250,000 mid-Atlantic households' figure.
